title: G2 RPO-A: Guided Group Relative Policy Optimization with Adaptive Guidance
abstract: This paper introduces G2 RPO-A, an adaptive algorithm that enhances the performance of small-size language models (SLMs) in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) by injecting ground-truth reasoning steps into roll-out trajectories. Our approach dynamically adjusts guidance length based on the model's real-time learning state, offering a sophisticated solution to the challenges of enhancing SLMs' performance in RLVR processes.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a complex math problem. You have a sequence of positive numbers, and you need to find the number in the sequence that is closest to 2013. Guidance can help you tackle this problem by providing high-quality thinking trajectories. However, simply adding guidance to the prompts (naive guidance) doesn't improve overall performance. We need to find a way to adaptively adjust guidance strength to achieve better results.

Let's explore how we can use guidance to improve the performance of small-size language models.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
The Guided Group Relative Policy Optimization (Guided GRPO) can be formulated as an optimization objective that incorporates guidance into the thinking trajectories. We investigate various design choices for guidance strategies, including the guidance ratio and guidance length. Our study examines the importance of hard training samples and finds that integrating these samples into the dataset using a curriculum learning approach significantly boosts the training efficiency of our method for SLMs.

We use a comprehensive analysis to find the optimal guidance configuration.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
We evaluate our method on mathematical reasoning and coding tasks with several models, including the Qwen3 series, DeepSeek-Math-7B-Base, and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Base. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed G2 RPO-A algorithm, achieving substantial performance gains over both vanilla GRPO and simple guided baselines. For example, on the MATH500 benchmark, G2 RPO-A achieves an accuracy of 87.15%, outperforming the base model (76.20%) and GRPO (85.37%).

Let's take a look at the benchmark results.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
The success of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) in large language models (LLMs) has been remarkable, but its effectiveness is significantly constrained when applied to smaller LLMs. Our approach addresses this limitation by providing a sophisticated solution to the challenges of enhancing small-size language models' performance in RLVR processes. This has significant implications for the development of more efficient and effective language models.

The impact of our approach is substantial.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
Our approach introduces several key innovations, including the use of adaptive guidance to adjust the guidance strength based on the model's real-time learning state. This allows for more effective use of guidance and improves the overall performance of the model. Additionally, our approach provides a comprehensive analysis of the effects of key guidance configurations, including the guidance ratio and guidance length.

These innovations have significant implications for the development of more efficient and effective language models.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To try out our approach, you can use the G2 RPO-A algorithm on your own language model. Simply implement the adaptive guidance mechanism and adjust the guidance strength based on the model's real-time learning state. You can also experiment with different guidance configurations to find the optimal setting for your specific use case.

Get started with G2 RPO-A today and see the improvements for yourself.
